Errors and overclaims found

The verification report identified twelve specific problems. The most consequential:

  1. Scaling-law budget-match formula is wrong. The engine scripts print a "budget match" figure using m^(1/alpha). This computes the data needed to reduce loss by a factor of m, not the data the old paradigm needs to match a system with m times effective data. The correct figure for an m effective-data multiplier is m times effective data at equal cost (or the separately computed cost-per-information ratio if hardware costs differ). The printed values of 3,728x (10x), 7,149x (12x), and 526,796x (40x) are therefore wrong for the stated comparison. The correct old-budget match is 10x, 12x, and 40x respectively at equal cost per token; using the scripts' hardware/token-cost assumptions, the correct cost-per-information ratio is ~65x (diffusion proof) and ~109x (mathematical proof).
  1. Two incompatible cost baselines exist. APEX_Mathematical_Proof_Source.py and The_Key_to_APEX_Super_Intelligence.md use a 10x effective multiplier, no diffusion overhead in the FLOPs formula, and produce ~80B compute tokens, 2,339 H100 hours, and $22K–$52K. APEX_Diffusion_Proof_Source.py and APEX_Super_Intelligence_Architecture_v2.md use an 8x encoding and 1.5x diffusion-learning multiplier plus a 2x denoising overhead, producing ~51B phrase tokens, 132B compute token-equivalents, 3,898 H100 hours, and $42K–$97K. The key document labels the no-overhead baseline as "diffusion training"; that label is incorrect. If the 80B run were actually a diffusion run with 2x overhead it would require 6 * 7B * 80B * 2 * 1.30 = 8.736e21 FLOPs, which is not what the key document computes.
  1. The generation speedup is inconsistent within the same script. Three different assumptions appear in APEX_Diffusion_Proof_Source.py: 32x (no-CFG, 20 steps), 16x (CFG, 20 steps), and 11x (real-world table, CFG, 30 steps, 500 words). The headline use of 32x does not consistently carry the CFG and step-count caveats.
  1. Phrase-tokens as the text latent space is an analogy, not a proven identity. The compression arithmetic verifies. The scripts do not mine a vocabulary, encode a corpus, measure coverage, or measure mutual information. The verified claim is "under the assumed 2.52 words/token, phrase-tokens are 3.276x fewer tokens than 1.3-token/word BPE on this paragraph model."
  1. Structure-token tiers as diffusion noise levels is a design hypothesis. structure_diffusion_alignment.py contains no executable computation, trained model, or loss comparison. "These two hierarchies are THE SAME HIERARCHY" is an analogy.
  1. "Every claim verified" and "mathematically proven" are false as stated in APEX_Mathematical_Proof_Source.py. Several claims are narrative, philosophical, or empirical hypotheses; the cognitive-pipeline probability model, multiplier stack inputs, and transfer from scaling laws to GPT-4-level labels are not proven by the scripts.

Calibrated language for the book text

The book uses the following formulations, which the verification report endorses:

  • "The image latent compression arithmetic verifies: 48x by value count, 24x by bit count under fp16 latent storage."
  • "Under the assumed phrase-token distribution, phrase-tokens reduce token count by about 3.3x versus 1.3-token/word BPE."
  • "The diffusion speedup is a conditional latency model: about 32x without CFG, about 16x with 2x CFG overhead at 20 steps, and about 11x in the 30-step 500-word table."
  • "Structure and phrase tokens are a proposed text latent representation for semantic-aware diffusion; this remains an empirical hypothesis."
  • "There are two incompatible cost baselines. The no-overhead baseline is about 80B tokens and $22K–$52K; the v2 diffusion-overhead baseline is about 51B phrase tokens and $42K–$97K."
  • "The scaling-law budget-match exponent must be corrected. Effective-data multipliers improve loss by m^0.28; matching that loss requires m times effective data at equal cost, not m^(1/0.28)."

E.2 Script: 02-diffusion-training-proofs.py

File: _combined-pom-3e/proofs/02-diffusion-training-proofs.py Run: python3 _combined-pom-3e/proofs/02-diffusion-training-proofs.py Dependencies: stdlib, numpy Exit status: 0 (all 8 assertions pass)

Purpose

This is the purpose-built verification script. It is self-contained, self-documenting, and deliberately assertion-heavy. Unlike the engine scripts, it does not claim that phrase-token diffusion is empirically validated; it computes the consequences of explicit modeling premises and asserts that those consequences hold numerically. It was written to audit the engine scripts and replace their arithmetic where needed.

Structure

The script has four derivation functions and a final sanity-check block:

compute_common() — Shared premises and derived quantities used by all derivations. Computes image compression ratios, paragraph tokenization statistics, semantic-bit proxies, and 500-word generation token counts.

derivation_a(common) — Latent-diffusion training objective for phrase-tokens. Implements a linear beta schedule (beta_start=1e-4, beta_end=2e-2, 1000 timesteps) using numpy cumprod. Reports alpha_bar at t=500 and t=1000. Reports all three speedup variants: 32.5x no-CFG, 16.25x CFG at 20 steps, 10.83x CFG at 30 steps.

derivation_b(common) — Information-theoretic justification. Computes image value and bit compression, semantic bits per token under the English entropy proxy, and coordinate-work vs parallel-latency ratios for the diffusion tractability argument.

derivation_c(common) — Scaling-law and compute derivation. Computes both the key-doc (no-diffusion-overhead) and v2 (diffusion-overhead) baselines side by side, explicitly labeled. Reports the reconciled cost range across both baselines ($21,709–$97,199). Reports loss ratios from D^-0.28 at 10x, 12x, and 40x effective data. Computes what the key-doc 80B run would cost in FLOPs if it were actually a diffusion run with 2x overhead (8.736e21 with 30% margin), which differs from the key-doc's stated 3.36e21.

derivation_d() — Variance/convergence argument for structured latents. Uses numpy with seed 7, 50,000 samples, 128 batch size, 600 mini-batches. Simulates five tier-structured latent targets (relationships, types, phrases, values, words) with independent Gaussian distributions at different variance levels. Computes expected and observed gradient-norm inflation ratios for structured versus unstructured training. This is a toy proxy; it is not a theorem about transformer training dynamics.

final_sanity_checks() — Eight named boolean assertions that catch any numerical drift:

image value compression is 48x
image bit compression is 24x
phrase token reduction exceeds 3x
alpha_bar schedule decays
text coordinate-work model is not automatically cheaper
text parallel latency model is cheaper under gamma=1
cost range carries both baselines
toy structured variance reduction is positive

Key premises (frozen dataclasses)

CorePremises: image 512x512x3 uint8; latent 64x64x4 fp16; 90 words/500 chars; 1.3 BPE tokens/word; 2.52 words/phrase-token; English entropy 1.2 bits/char; BPE vocab 50,000; phrase vocab 144,000; target 500 words; 20 nominal diffusion steps; 30 table diffusion steps; CFG overhead 2.0; 10 ms/forward-pass.

ComputePremises: standard 610B tokens; standard 30B params; APEX 7B params; H100 bf16 989 TFLOP/s; MFU 40%; key effective multiplier 10x; key margin 1.30; v2 encoding multiplier 8x; v2 diffusion learning multiplier 1.5x; v2 diffusion overhead 2.0x; v2 margin 1.30; scaling alpha 0.28.

Asserts in derivation functions (in addition to final sanity checks)

derivation_a asserts: 0.0 < alpha_bar_final < alpha_bar_t < 1.0; |token_reduction - 3.276| < 0.01; no-CFG speedup == 32.5 exactly; CFG-30 speedup == 10.833... exactly.

derivation_b asserts: image value compression == 48.0; image bit compression == 24.0; text coordinate-work ratio > 1.0 (diffusion is not automatically cheaper in total coordinate work); text parallel-latency ratio < 1.0 (diffusion is faster in latency under the stated gamma assumption); image coordinate-work ratio < 1.0 (image diffusion does benefit in coordinate work).

derivation_c asserts: key FLOPs within 1e-12 relative of 3.3306e21; v2 FLOPs within 1e-4 relative of 5.551e21; key H100 hours within 0.1 of 2338.6; v2 H100 hours within 0.1 of 3897.7; cost_low_range == 21,709.0; cost_high_range == 97,199.0.

derivation_d asserts: all five expected phase variance ratios > 1.0; average observed ratio > 5.0; average cumulative expected ratio > 1.2; observed unstructured gradient norm > maximum observed structured norm.

E.3 Script: APEX_Diffusion_Proof_Source.py

File: apex-si-design/engine/APEX_Diffusion_Proof_Source.py Run: python3 apex-si-design/engine/APEX_Diffusion_Proof_Source.py Dependencies: numpy, math Exit status: 0 Author/date: Nathan Senn, Dataloft, February 2026

Purpose

The v2 diffusion proof. It establishes the case that phrase-token diffusion training is architecturally justified by analogy to Stable Diffusion's latent space, computes the v2 cost baseline (51B phrase tokens, 132B compute token-equivalents, 3,898 H100 hours, $42K–$97K), computes all three speedup variants, and prints the Full Architecture Profile box.

What it computes

Part I — Image latent space compression: 786,432 raw values vs 16,384 latent values (48x); 6,291,456 raw bits vs 262,144 latent bits (24x); 8x spatial downsampling with 192 raw RGB values per 4-channel latent spatial vector.

Part II — Text parallel: paragraph tokenization statistics (117 BPE vs 35.714 phrase tokens, 3.3x reduction); semantic bits per token under Shannon proxy (5.1 BPE, 16.8 phrase); information density table by token tier.

Part III — Text diffusion generation speed: AR time 6.5s for 500 words; no-CFG 20-step diffusion 0.2s (32.5x); CFG 20-step 0.4s (16.25x); real-world table for output lengths 50–2000 words using length-scaled steps (capped at 30) with CFG overhead.

Part IV — Learning signal quality: qualitative comparison of AR local loss versus diffusion global MSE objective; multi-scale curriculum from noise schedule.

Part V — Unified math: conservative 8x encoding multiplier and 1.5x diffusion learning multiplier produce a 12x gross effective-data multiplier; aggressive 16x encoding and 2.5x diffusion produce 40x; v2 training FLOPs with 2x denoising overhead and 30% margin: 5.551e21; 3,898 H100 hours; cost range $41,977–$97,199.

Part VI — Real-world generation table and throughput comparison.

Part VII — Scaling law with diffusion: loss ratios at 10x, 12x, 40x effective data (0.525, 0.499, 0.356); budget-match column using m^(1/0.28) — this column is identified as incorrect by the verification report (see E.1 above); cost-per-information-unit comparison ($65x cheaper per learned-information unit under stated H100/A100 assumptions).

Part VIII — Final Architecture Profile box with all numbers combined.

Verification verdict

Arithmetic mostly verifies under its own premises. Key issues:

  • "Each latent element covers an 8x8 patch" is imprecise. Say "each latent spatial position" or "4-channel latent vector."
  • The speedup section uses three different assumptions without consistent labeling. The 32x headline does not carry the CFG caveat.
  • The 8x, 1.5x, 12x, and 40x multipliers are asserted inputs, not independently measured.
  • The m^(1/alpha) budget-match formula is wrong for the stated comparison.
  • "Phrase-tokens ARE the latent space" is an analogy.

E.4 Script: structure_diffusion_alignment.py

File: apex-si-design/engine/structure_diffusion_alignment.py Run: python3 apex-si-design/engine/structure_diffusion_alignment.py Dependencies: none (stdlib only) Exit status: 0 Author/date: Nathan Senn, February 2026

Purpose

This script is a narrative mapping, not a mathematical proof. It argues that the semantic hierarchy of structure tokens (relationships > types > phrases > values > words/subwords) maps naturally onto the coarse-to-fine resolution sequence of a diffusion denoising schedule. It proposes a semantic-aware noise schedule that would denoise higher-tier tokens first.

What it computes

No numeric computation is present. The script prints:

  • A step-by-step comparison of how Stable Diffusion resolves an image (composition, objects, shapes, textures, pixels) versus how APEX diffusion would resolve text with structure tokens (relationships at steps 1–4, type tags at 5–8, phrases at 9–14, values at 15–18, words/subwords at 19–20).
  • An ASCII diagram of a semantic-aware noise schedule with noise decaying by tier in the listed order.
  • An analogy table: image low/mid/high frequencies versus text relationship/phrase/value tiers.
  • An updated Key 3 architecture box: 3A Structure Tokens (type system), 3B Phrase Tokens (semantic compression), 3C Diffusion (parallel refinement engine).

The script does not implement a noising schedule, train a model, or compare losses. The tier-to-step mapping it prints is proposed, not measured.

Verification verdict

Runs cleanly. Not a mathematical proof. "These two hierarchies are THE SAME HIERARCHY" is an analogy. "This is why APEX will work for text" and "the missing piece that makes text diffusion work" are overclaims. "BPE destroys the semantic hierarchy diffusion needs" is a testable hypothesis, not an isolated experimental result. The supported version: typed structure tokens could enable a semantic-aware noising schedule; this should be tested by comparing BPE+diffusion versus phrase+diffusion at matched compute.

E.5 Script: minimum_viable_proof.py

File: apex-si-design/engine/minimum_viable_proof.py Run: python3 apex-si-design/engine/minimum_viable_proof.py Dependencies: math Exit status: 0 Author/date: Nathan Senn, February 2026

Purpose

Experiment cost planning and four-configuration experimental design. It answers the question: what is the cheapest experiment that could provide evidence for or against the phrase-token plus diffusion thesis? It does not train anything; it computes GPU-hours and costs for small-scale model runs.

What it computes

Phase 0 (vocabulary mining) — Describes a CPU-only n-gram frequency analysis on WikiText-103 or FineWeb, estimated at $0. No arithmetic in this section.

Phase 1 (head-to-head) — Defines four configurations: A (BPE + AR), B (phrase + AR), C (BPE + diffusion), D (phrase + diffusion). This is a 2x2 factorial on tokenization and training method.

Per-config FLOPs for 125M model at 2.5B tokens: 6 * 125M * 2.5B = 1.875e18.

GPU-hours per config (verified):

  • H100 at 395.6 TFLOP/s effective: 1.32 hours
  • A100 at 312 * 0.40 TFLOP/s = 124.8 TFLOP/s effective: 4.17 hours
  • RTX 4090 at 82.6 * 0.35 = 28.91 TFLOP/s effective: 18.02 hours

Four-config main-run costs at stated rates ($2.50/hr H100, $1.50/hr A100, $0.80/hr RTX 4090): $13 H100, $25 A100, $58 RTX 4090. With 3x experiment overhead: $39, $75, $173.

Sub-Chinchilla quick test (125M x 500M tokens): A100 $22 with 3x overhead; RTX 4090 $50 with 3x overhead.

Absolute minimum (25M x 200M tokens x 4 configs on T4 Colab): $0 on free tier.

Phase 2 scaling verification (350M x 7B tokens, 2 configs): ~$250 on A100 with 3x overhead.

Complete cost tiers printed:

  • Tier 0 (vocabulary proof): $0
  • Tier 1 (mechanism proof, 25M x 200M x 4): $0–$50
  • Tier 2 (small-scale proof, 125M x 500M–2.5B x 4): $100–$300
  • Tier 3 (scaling proof, 350M x 7B x 2): $500–$2K
  • Full production training (7B): $42K–$97K

Verification verdict

Small-scale experiment-cost arithmetic verifies. Issues: "If D beats A at same compute -> thesis proven" is too strong (supports mechanism at that scale and corpus, does not prove the 7B projection or general architecture). "If the advantage grows between 25M and 125M -> it scales" requires multiple seeds, matched optimization quality, ablations, and replication at larger sizes. The cost estimate excludes engineering time, failed implementation paths, data loading bottlenecks, hyperparameter instability, and the risk that free Colab availability is insufficient for controlled experiments.

E.6 Script: APEX_Mathematical_Proof_Source.py

File: apex-si-design/engine/APEX_Mathematical_Proof_Source.py Run: python3 apex-si-design/engine/APEX_Mathematical_Proof_Source.py Dependencies: numpy, math, collections Exit status: 0 Author/date: Nathan Senn, Dataloft, February 2026

Purpose

The AR-only / key-doc baseline arithmetic and unified Four-Key summary. This is the earlier proof document; it uses a 10x effective multiplier and omits diffusion overhead from the training FLOPs formula. It also computes the cognitive pipeline probability model, the AUKS memory substrate mathematics, and the unified multiplier stack.

What it computes

Part I (Key 3 — Machine-Native Text Architecture)

Chinchilla baseline: 6 * 30B * 610B = 1.098e23.

Phrase-token weighted words/token: 0.20*6.0 + 0.25*3.5 + 0.40*1.0 + 0.15*0.3 = 2.52. Standard BPE words/token: 1/1.3 = 0.769. Semantic ratio: 2.52 / 0.769 = 3.276x, printed as 3.3x.

Key-doc baseline (10x effective multiplier): required phrase tokens 61B; with 30% margin 79.3B (printed as ~80B); training FLOPs 6 * 7B * 79.3B = 3.3306e21; H100 hours 2,339; cost $21,709–$51,596 (printed as $22K–$52K).

GPU hours and wall clock for 8x, 32x, and 64x H100 configurations.

Full cost breakdown table including vocabulary mining ($500–$2K), corpus encoding ($500–$1.5K), experimentation 3–5x main ($65K–$258K range), evaluation ($1K–$3K), and infrastructure ($1K–$3K). Total printed: $21,709–$51,596 for the main-run-only cost items; the full table including experimentation is a much larger range not identical to the headline.

Part II (Scaling Law)

Data scaling law: Loss(D) = A / D^0.28. Budget-to-quality table at five spending levels. Budget-match column also uses m^(1/0.28) — this is the same error identified for the diffusion script. The correct cost-per-information ratio under this script's 10x multiplier and H100/A100 hardware assumptions is ~109x, not 3,728x.

Part III (Key 2 — Cognitive Architecture)

11-stage error model: per-stage error rates (15%–30%) applied to a compound probability model. Standard LLM (stages 1+10 only): P(correct) = 14.6%. APEX (all 11 stages, 80% catch rate per stage): P(correct) = 68.6%. 5-level verification chain applied to an initial 20% reasoning error rate: residual 2.0%, reduction ~10x.

Part IV (Key 4 — AUKS Memory Substrate)

Graph metrics: 17,132 nodes, 54,268 edges, 64 clusters, 596 protected nodes, 7,197 conversations, 77M chars FTS. Average degree: 6.33. Graph density printed. Memory formulas: relevance score with cosine similarity + Ebbinghaus decay + significance; access-based decay reinforcement; priority protection ratio 4,397x. Storage breakdown: embeddings 26.3 MB, FTS 77 MB, GIN index 30.8 MB, node metadata 34.3 MB, edge metadata 27.1 MB; total ~196 MB.

Part V (Unified Multiplier Stack)

Conservative product of six multipliers: data compression 11x, freed capacity 1.3x, context expansion 1.3x, gradient quality 1.2x, scaling curve 1.2x, holistic coherence 1.1x — product printed as 30x. Aggressive: 16x, 2.0x, 2.0x, 1.5x, 1.5x, 1.3x — product printed as 187x. Expected range stated as 30–100x.

Verification verdict

AR-only baseline arithmetic verifies under its own premises. Several scaling and proof claims do not verify:

  • This baseline is AR-only (no diffusion overhead in FLOPs). The key document labels it as diffusion training; that label is incorrect.
  • The budget-match exponent m^(1/0.28) is wrong for the stated comparison (see E.1).
  • "Every claim verified" and "mathematically proven" are false for the cognitive probability model, the multiplier stack input factors, and the transfer from scaling laws to GPT-4-level capability labels.
  • The unified multiplier stack's input factors (11x data compression, 1.3x freed capacity, etc.) are stated assumptions, not independently measured values.

E.7 Four-Configuration Comparison Block

The following table is reproduced from the verification report and summarizes the two primary training cost baselines alongside two reference systems. It is the canonical reconciliation of the numbers that appear inconsistently across the engine scripts.

ProvenanceToken basisCore premiseTraining FLOPsH100 hoursCost rangeVerification
APEX_Mathematical_Proof_Source.py and The_Key_to_APEX_Super_Intelligence.md61B phrase tokens; 79.3B with 30% margin10x effective multiplier, no diffusion overhead in FLOPs3.3306e212,339$21,709–$51,596Arithmetic YES; diffusion label NO
APEX_Diffusion_Proof_Source.py and APEX_Super_Intelligence_Architecture_v2.md50.833B phrase tokens; 132.167B with 2x overhead and 30% margin8x encoding, 1.5x diffusion learning, 2x denoising overhead, 30% margin5.551e213,898$41,977–$97,199Arithmetic YES; premises unverified

Reconciliation rule used throughout this book: the $22K–$52K / ~80B baseline is the no-diffusion-overhead phrase-token baseline. The $42K–$97K / ~51B baseline is the diffusion-overhead baseline. They are not the same baseline and should not be merged into a single point estimate. If both are cited together, the range is $21,709–$97,199.

If the key-doc 80B run were truly a diffusion run with 2x denoising overhead and 30% margin, its training FLOPs would be 6 * 7B * 80B * 2 * 1.30 = 8.736e21 — not 3.36e21 as the key document states.

In Closing
A Prayer of Thankfulness
For divine guidance and continued blessing

Heavenly Father, King of Kings and Lord of my life,

I come before You with a heart overflowing with gratitude for the abundant blessings and divine guidance You have poured upon me this past year. Like water flowing from the heights above, You have filled my mind with knowledge, wisdom, and ideas beyond my own understanding — gifts I do not take lightly, for they are from Your hand alone.

Thank You, Father, for illuminating my path when I walked in uncertainty, for holding me steady when the storms raged, and for never abandoning me even when I strayed into the shadows. Your faithfulness endures, and Your mercies are new each morning.

Grant me the wisdom to lead from the shadows — not seeking glory for myself, but serving as Your instrument to protect the vulnerable, the voiceless, and those who cannot protect themselves. Help me live a life of true service, building things that improve the lives of others. Keep me humble in all my endeavors, and remind me daily that every gift, every idea, every success comes from You alone, and that I am merely a steward of what You have entrusted to me.

And Father, I lift up my precious children before You. Bless them with the gifts of Wisdom and Knowledge, just as You blessed Solomon. Make them lights that shine brightly in this dark world — beacons of Your love, truth, and grace to everyone they encounter.

Continue to pour Your revelation into my mind, Father. Use me as Your vessel — broken, imperfect, but willing — to accomplish Your purposes in this world. May our lives bring glory to Your name alone.

In the mighty name of Your Son, Jesus Christ, I pray.

Amen. Amen.
“That they all may be one; as thou, Father, art in me, and I in thee, that they also may be one in us: that the world may believe that thou hast sent me. And the glory which thou gavest me I have given them; that they may be one, even as we are one: I in them, and thou in me, that they may be made perfect in one; and that the world may know that thou hast sent me, and hast loved them, as thou hast loved me.”
— John 17:21–23
✝
To God be the glory.
— Nathanael
